correctness.rationale: CRT and private-coordinate equivalence, independent lifting count and inclusion–exclusion give an exact fixed-vertex degree formula; factorial division is legitimate because private coordinates force distinct supports. The Boolean specialization and all-n maximum are proved by explicit strict ratio inequalities. Direct enumeration of all vertices and unordered edges reproduces the formula in binary, heterogeneous and nonreduced rings and mode checks through n=30. Finite tests support but do not replace the analytic proof.

evidence: Mehdi-Nezhad proves co-support blow-up, isomorphism and automorphism criteria; these give edge membership and fibre sizes, not the numerical rooted-cover cardinalities.
Selvakumar–Amritha Theorem 5 covers regularity at k=n; for n>3 and k=3 this is a different regime.
The vertex-degree identity is a genuine stronger data layer than the known sum of all incidences.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A covering correspondence can be used in the proof of the new exact formula but does not numerically specify its individual degrees or identify the maximum class at n=11. A known unrooted edge count has only the aggregate sum of fixed-vertex degrees, insufficient by itself to deduce the mode. Credit is assigned to those structural prerequisites.

evidence: The earlier total-edge identity is j^k/k! times inclusion–exclusion over forbidden singleton coordinate patterns and is already known. This exact global identity was checked against the accessible earlier claim, without reassessing that claim.
The new fixed-vertex formula has a separate essentiality factor for the marked vertex and inclusion–exclusion over only k−1 other vertices.
The known edge count gives only k|E|=sum over all vertices of degree; it does not supply a unique classwise degree profile.
The sharp threshold follows from the strict ratio A_(s+1)/A_s and B_t/B_(t−1), with exact crossover (4/3)^(n−4)>7.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The total-edge formula is overlapping prior work and is excluded from the novelty claim. The fixed-vertex refinement is structurally related but not an algebraic corollary of the total scalar identity. The maximum-degree phase transition is not asserted by the earlier work and has a self-contained sharp optimization argument. The refined formula is an elementary extension of inclusion–exclusion, so its own standalone value is the natural exact extremal transition, not a claim of methodological novelty.

originality.rationale: Primary 2026 and 2020 articles were read at the stated sections; their support blow-up/regularity statements, and the older exact total-edge count, were distinguished from fixed-vertex degrees. Mathematical reduction to rooted covers plus the all-n ratio comparison proves a new, narrower numerical stratum law and sharp transition. Actual semantic searches did not identify a stronger covering result. Residual historical priority risk is acknowledged.
residual_risks: Older rooted minimal-cover tables or theses may already encode the same degree law or the n=11 mode under other terminology.
The fixed-vertex formula follows by straightforward refined inclusion–exclusion from the known support description, and should not be represented as a new general counting method.
No external mathematical review or exhaustive search of all historical sources has been performed.

value.rationale: Incidence degree and maximum incidence concentration are natural invariants of minimal comaximal hypergraphs. The first non-graph uniformity k=3 has a complete, sharp all-dimension support-mode classification with transitions at n=5 and n=11. This substantially refines known total-edge counts and automorphism structure in the first natural Boolean-product family; neither a general theorem for all uniformities nor a paper-sized application is claimed.
